title: Disaster Tweets private-data comparison (blocked candidate)
summary: Candidate private-input package comparing unigram Naive Bayes with adjacent word pairs on identical train-only folds; no actual competition inputs supplied.
split_definition: Five target-stratified folds with seed 17; exact normalized duplicate texts rejected; vocabulary and class counts fit training rows only.
metric: positive-class F1 (zero when denominator is zero)
environment: Declared target: Python 3.12.14 standard library on Darwin arm64; no actual Disaster Tweets run recorded. Set private input/output environment variables as documented before execution.
steps: Obtain authorized private training and optional test files outside Git/public; inspect current access/rules.
Use the pinned package and declare duplicate policy before scoring; do not silently deduplicate to pass.
Compare unchanged unigram/pair models on the same five train-only folds; inspect aggregate confusion and private local errors.
Compare notebook/script metrics exactly; locally validate a private submission without uploading.
limitations: No actual Disaster Tweets competition data has been supplied or executed; generated tests cannot satisfy actual-data acceptance.
Exact token-normalized duplicates are rejected without silent deletion; near-duplicates and grouped-template leakage remain limitations.
Random stratification does not group events, users or time.
Mean fold F1 is distinct from pooled OOF and hidden competition test F1.
Raw text, user-supplied IDs and local error excerpts stay private.
Traced allocations are not RSS; no actual learner compute budget measured.

project.outcome: Explain a train-only text feature comparison, positive-class F1 and false-positive/negative patterns without publishing raw texts.
prerequisites: Run a local Python script and set private environment variables.
Explain binary targets, positive-class F1 and the vocabulary fitting boundary.

access.instructions: Inspect https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nlp-getting-started/data and current rules yourself; obtain authorized train.csv and optional test.csv privately. Follow docs/nlp-actual-data-setup.md; no automatic acquisition or submission.
access.authorization: Missing: no authorized learner-supplied competition inputs or access evidence received.

project.baseline: Fit unigram Naive Bayes vocabulary and counts inside each fixed stratified training fold.
project.controlled_change: Add adjacent word pairs with unchanged smoothing, threshold and folds; retain worse outcomes.
diagnostics: Does adding adjacent word pairs help consistently across the same five fixed stratified folds?
What do aggregate false positives/negatives and repeated-template overlap omit about transfer?
